subject: Subservice carve-out mapping, bridge letter, and subprocessor evidence for AegisCloud review
messages:
From: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@aegiscloud.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Bennett <lisa.bennett@aegiscloud.com>, sec-team@aegiscloud.com
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 16:10:00 -0400
Subject: Questions on carve-outs / SOC2 period coverage for Redwood

Jonas —

Thanks for taking this. We're running through Redwood as part of AegisCloud's vendor security evaluation for our data platform integration. A few specific asks up front so our InfoSec team can progress: 

- Can you confirm the SOC 2 Type II report period Redwood has available (start/end dates)? We need a period that overlaps our audit window (2026-09-01 through 2027-03-31).
- If Redwood relies on cloud provider SOC reports as subservice org carve-outs, can you provide a mapping (which cloud reports + which controls are carved out) and any bridge-letter language you typically provide?
- Please send an export of current subprocessors (name, role, datacenter region) and indicate which ones are included in Redwood's SOC coverage versus those that are out-of-scope.
- KMS / key custody — do you offer customer-managed KMS options and can you provide evidence (diagram or statement) showing who holds keys for production tenant data?

We attached our security questionnaire (SIG-lite) to speed things up. Ideally we'd get the documents by EOD Monday so InfoSec can review ahead of a short risk committee meeting next week. Happy to set a call if that helps.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Hargreaves
Security Program Manager
AegisCloud
Attachment: Aegis_Security_Questionnaire_v3.pdf

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@aegiscloud.com>
Cc: Lisa Bennett <lisa.bennett@aegiscloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 17:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Questions on carve-outs / SOC2 period coverage for Redwood

Tom —

Appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers and next steps below; looping in Marissa from our security & compliance team to provide the artifact set and the KMS custody mapping.

1) SOC 2 Type II period: our most recent Type II report covers 2026-01-01 through 2026-12-31. We can provide the full report (PDF) and an executive summary now. If your window needs later coverage, we can discuss a bridge letter to extend assurance for the interim period; I'll include our typical bridge-letter language.

2) Subservice carve-outs: Redwood uses both AWS and GCP as subservice organizations. We leverage their SOC reports for infrastructure controls; however, application-level controls, access provisioning, and product change controls are in-scope for Redwood. We'll provide a mapping CSV that shows which provider report we rely on and which control families are carved out.

3) Subprocessor inventory: attaching a current export (subprocessor_inventory_20270401.csv). It includes role and region and a flag for "covered-by-Redwood-SOC". If you need more granularity (contact or contract dates), let us know.

4) KMS custody: we support two modes — customer-managed KMS (recommended) where customers supply a key in their cloud account, and Redwood-managed KMS where we hold the CMK in a Redwood tenant. We'll send a short custody mapping document and the KM practice slide.

Next steps: Marissa will attach the SOC2 PDF, the mapping CSV, and a draft bridge-letter text. If Aegis wants signature-level bridge letters we can route that internally — agree that a short 30-min call will accelerate. Are you available Mon 4/5 at 10am ET or Tue 4/6 at 2pm ET?

Jonas
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@aegiscloud.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Bennett <lisa.bennett@aegiscloud.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 04 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Questions on carve-outs / SOC2 period coverage for Redwood

Hi Tom —

Attaching the artifacts Jonas mentioned:
- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026-report.pdf (full report)
- subprocessor_inventory_20270401.csv (current inventory; column "covered_by_soc" indicates scope)
- kms-custody-mapping-20270402.pdf (illustrates customer-managed vs Redwood-managed key flows)

A few clarifications that may help your reviewers: 
- Cloud provider carve-outs: we rely on AWS SOC and GCP SOC reports for infrastructure physical/host-level controls only. We do not carve out logical access, change management for our application, or product data processing controls. The CSV maps control categories (e.g., CC6, CC7) to whether they are Redwood-owned or covered via provider.
- Bridge letter: below is the boilerplate we usually propose for interim coverage when the report period doesn't align. If Aegis needs it on corporate letterhead or notarized, please flag that and we'll route to Legal.

--- draft bridge-letter excerpt ---
Redwood Inference maintains a SOC 2 Type II report covering the period 2026-01-01 through 2026-12-31. To the extent that Redwood relies on third-party subservice organizations for physical and infrastructure controls, Redwood confirms these dependencies and provides mapping to the respective subservice SOC reports. For the period following the above report and until Redwood's subsequent Type II report is issued, Redwood confirms that no material changes were made to its control environment affecting [relevant control families], and Redwood will promptly notify the customer of any material control changes.
--- end excerpt ---

- KMS: the kms-custody PDF spells out production defaults and options. For customers opting for customer-managed KMS, Redwood never holds the CMK; for Redwood-managed keys we hold the CMK and restrict access via a documented key custody process that is available as evidence.

If it's helpful, Rishi can provide a short attestation table showing which subprocessors are included in Redwood's SOC scope vs. those covered by separate contractual assurances. Rishi — can you take that?

Happy to jump on the call Jonas suggested; Mon 4/5 10am ET works for me.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026-report.pdf, subprocessor_inventory_20270401.csv, kms-custody-mapping-20270402.pdf

From: Lisa Bennett <lisa.bennett@aegiscloud.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@aegiscloud.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Questions on carve-outs / SOC2 period coverage for Redwood

Thanks all — this is exactly what we needed to move forward. I reviewed the SOC report and the subprocessor inventory; a couple quick asks before our risk committee: 

- Please confirm whether Redwood has any subcontractors that process customer data in APAC regions (we need region-level coverage).
- For the bridge letter, we require explicit mention that there were no material changes to access controls or key custody practices since 2026-12-31. The draft excerpt looks fine but please make that explicit language if possible.

We're good to take the call Mon 4/5 10am ET — Tom, Marissa, Jonas, please share a calendar invite and a dial-in. If the bridge letter can be provided as a signed PDF by EOD Tue 4/6, that will let our committee sign-off and close the vendor assessment.

Lisa Bennett
Head of Vendor Risk
AegisCloud
